condition: Gastric carcinoma (weight loss with upper abdominal pain)
summary: 61-year-old woman with 2 months of epigastric pain, early satiety and 6 kg unintentional weight loss; no dysphagia. NG12: aged ≥55 with weight loss and upper abdominal pain → urgent OGD within 2 weeks.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Upper abdominal pain and weight loss
inputs.hpi: Two months of gnawing upper abdominal pain, feeling full after a few mouthfuls and loss of appetite. Lost 6 kg without trying. Swallowing is normal. Not taking anti-inflammatories. Mother had stomach cancer.

exam.general: Thin. Mild conjunctival pallor. No supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
exam.abdomen: Mild epigastric tenderness, no palpable mass, no hepatomegaly.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired seamstress. Never smoked. Family history: mother — gastric cancer at 70.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected gastric carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Epigastric pain, early satiety and 6 kg weight loss aged 61 with microcytic anaemia and raised platelets — suspected gastric carcinoma. Urgent 2-week-wait OGD.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: cholecystitis, peptic ulcer, GORD — weight_loss/anorexia do not outweigh the cholecystitis prior (×2 female, ×1.6 age 30–70). Symptom inference, passive ranking and triageSurgical all rank gastric carcinoma #1.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: pane-engine modifiers: age ≥55 multiplier for gastric/oesophageal carcinoma (as colorectal has); consider weight_loss likelihoods.

emergencyLevel.note: Red flag, not an emergency: urgent (2-week) outpatient endoscopy. CLAUDE.md: red flags warrant expedited outpatient review, not ER redirect.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (oesophageal and stomach cancer)
guideline.section: Offer urgent direct access upper GI endoscopy (within 2 weeks) to assess for oesophageal or stomach cancer in people with dysphagia (any age), or aged ≥55 with weight loss and any of upper abdominal pain, reflux or dyspepsia; consider urgent OGD in people aged ≥55 with upper abdominal pain and low haemoglobin, or raised platelets with upper abdominal pain
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (last updated 2023).

guideline.name: NICE CG184 — Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
guideline.section: Alarm features: refer under NG12 rather than empirical treatment
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG184. London: NICE; 2014 (last updated 2019).

rationale: Red flag without dysphagia: the age-55 weight-loss criterion of NG12, with anaemia and thrombocytosis as supporting features. Tests that engines reach gastric cancer and urgent OGD from epigastric pain plus weight loss.
